input_source: Published original reviewer comments only; TP/FP adjudications excluded from runtime inputs

findings.review_message: `volume = m.volume_24h if m.volume_24h > 0 else m.volume` falls back to the lifetime cumulative `volume` field when `volume_24h` is zero. Any market with nonzero historical cumulative volume (even if completely inactive for months) will satisfy `has_volume >= volume_floor` and never be considered stale. This makes the fallback path counterproductive: it's intended to handle missing 24h data but actually permanently exempts high-history dead markets from staleness filtering.
findings.contract_context: Zero recent 24h volume, unchanged price and unchanged OI must count as inactive despite historic cumulative volume

findings.review_message: `oi_changed = oi != entry.get("open_interest", 0)` defaults the missing field to 0. On first load of an old `scan_staleness.json` (without `open_interest`), every market with nonzero OI — essentially all real markets — will have `oi_changed=True`, resetting their accumulated stale count to 0. This silently voids all previously-built-up staleness state on migration, making the filter ineffective for another full `staleness_cycles` rounds.
findings.contract_context: Whether old counter resets on schema migration are acceptable requires a separate migration contract

findings.review_message: `has_volume = volume >= volume_floor` checks current absolute volume against a fixed floor, not whether trading activity changed between cycles. A market with a consistently stagnant 10-15 contracts/day will never accumulate a stale count and will never be filtered, even though it is essentially dead. The old `volume_spike_ratio` checked for a relative increase in volume (i.e., actual new activity) — the replacement checks only for presence of volume above a minimum, conflating "some volume exists" with "trading just happened".
findings.contract_context: Whether the floor should be relative is a maintainer policy decision; present targeted tests encode absolute floor
